task_text: Supported cube flip relay: The left arm holds a large shallow tray with a cube on it, and the right arm holds a small flat pusher. The left arm must first bring the tray to a presentation point. The right arm must then tip the cube over onto an adjacent face. It does so with a short push that sets the cube rotating and ends before the cube is half-way over, so that the cube completes the tip on its own momentum and settles on the tray. The left arm then moves the cube, on the tray, to a new place, and the pusher tips it a second time in the same way, so that the cube's original bottom face ends up on top. Finally the tray must carry the correctly oriented cube to an output point and hold it there. The cube must never leave the tray. Phases, in order: support_presentation: the cube is on the tray (it has touched the tray's tool link within the last 25 ms) while the tray's tool frame is within 0.025 m of the presentation point (0.08, 0.015, 0.23).; first_inertial_flip: an inertial flip, judged only from pusher contacts made in this phase. The tilt of a cube axis means the angle between that cube-local axis and world vertical; here the tilted axis is the cube's local z (initially up). (a) The pusher (any part of its tool link) touches the cube; the tilt at the last moment of contact is the release angle. (b) Early release: at some moment more than 0.02 s after the last pusher contact, the cube is untouched by the pusher, the release angle was between 0.03 rad and pi/4 - 0.02 = 0.765 rad (about 1.7 to 43.9 deg), and the cube turns faster than 0.4 rad/s. This is recorded once. (c) Inertial crossing: after the early release, the tilt grows from at most 45 deg (pi/4) at one physics step to more than 45 deg at the next. (d) After that, the final state must hold for 0.25 s without interruption: the cube's local +x axis (the face that initially faced +x, toward the right arm) points up within 0.18 rad (about 10.3 deg), the cube moves slower than 0.05 m/s and turns slower than 0.3 rad/s, and it is on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms). The cube's world position at the moment this phase completes is recorded.; second_contact_geometry: with the cube on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms) and not touched by the pusher at that moment, the cube's centre is more than 0.025 m (world distance) away from the position recorded at the end of first_inertial_flip.; second_inertial_flip: the same inertial-flip rule as first_inertial_flip, judged only from pusher contacts made in this phase, with the cube's local x axis (now pointing up) as the tilted axis. That is: a pusher contact, then a release with tilt between 0.03 rad and 0.765 rad followed (more than 0.02 s later, still untouched) by an angular speed above 0.4 rad/s, then the tilt of local x passing 45 deg. The final state is that the cube's local -z axis (its original bottom face) points up within 0.18 rad, with speed < 0.05 m/s, angular speed < 0.3 rad/s and the cube on the tray, for 0.25 s without interruption.; oriented_output: for 0.5 s without interruption: the cube is on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms) and its local -z axis points up within 0.18 rad; the tray's tool frame is within 0.025 m of the output point (-0.04, 0.16, 0.25); and the cube moves at less than 0.04 m/s relative to the tray. This completes the task. Goal geometry: Presentation point (0.08, 0.015, 0.23) for the tray's tool frame (support_presentation); output point (-0.04, 0.16, 0.25) for the tray's tool frame (oriented_output).
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where the task has succeeded (every phase in order) or failed (a failure event, a forbidden contact, a safety-limit violation, an object out of bounds, or the task's horizon of 25 s of simulated time, 2500 control steps), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
